title: All Cookie documentation is gone
body:
Example: http://docs.guzzlephp.org/en/latest/request-options.html?highlight=cookie#cookies

Everything is gone. Search the whole docs for "cookie" and "cookies":

- http://docs.guzzlephp.org/en/latest/search.html?q=cookie&check_keywords=yes&area=default
- http://docs.guzzlephp.org/en/latest/search.html?q=cookies&check_keywords=yes&area=default

None of the links work. The cookies have been eradicated from the docs. ;-) Seems to have been this way for a while. 5.3 docs lack it too.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: Can you elaborate? How are the docs gone? You provided a link directly to the cookie docs.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
@mtdowling Ehhh... I tested other browsers. Okay, I see no cookies section in the example link on my desktop, Google Chrome and Safari on a Mac. Neither shows any cookie section.

But Safari on iOS on an iPhone 5 is able to see it...

This is what the page looks like on desktop (cookies is supposed to be between these two items):

![screen shot 2017-03-03 at 16 46 15](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/22373193/23557648/f9aabea6-0030-11e7-8fdf-be7fc1f10db7.png)

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: Can you see it in the navigation?

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: Hey @SteveJobzniak, sounds like a dupe of #1401 .

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
Oh I think it's the Prebake adblock filter which hides all EU cookie notices.

This shows the danger of calling the section "cookies" and making it a prime target of various browser addons...

I guess renaming it is out of the question since the docs are autogenerated?

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body:
> This shows the danger of calling the section "cookies" and making it a prime target of various browser addons...

Mhhm, let me imagine the issues which will be open if the section was named "Kekse", "Småkage" or "biscuits". `Cookie` is a well-known name for the concept it describes. 

But because it interests me: Which name would you suggest?

comments.author: Participant 4
Participant 1
comments.body:
From the above, the best solution seems to be to just rewrite the documentation markup a little bit, to use an anchor with a name instead of another element with an "id", since ad-blockers target "id" but not "name": ```html

Cookies

text here... ``` That was confirmed working. You can jump to such named anchors via `#cookies` in the URL bar. And since there's no "src" on the anchor, it won't cause the browser to draw it as a hyperlink with underlines. It's also possible to just do `

Cookies

` but I heard that's invalid XHTML (which is what you serve the docs as).

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body:
How do we want to proceed here?

1. Take the solution from @SteveJobzniak 
2. Add a hint to the documentation
3. Both

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: I am not a huge fan of either of those TBH.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: The <a> anchor name solution preserves all old links (#cookies) and is a valid way to write anchors. It existed in HTML before CSS IDs existed. So my vote goes to that solution.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: Rewriting the doc markup seems way overkill for this, especially since the docs are generated using Sphinx.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
@mtdowling Oh so it's a 3rd party doc generator...

Ehh, then I don't know what to do. They're unlikely to change markup just because your project has a "cookies" id/heading.

Perhaps add a notice about disabling adblocker while reading the docs to ensure the cookies section isn't hidden?

It would have to be a small info box at the top of the "Request Options" page to be seen.

The "cookies" link under Request Options goes nowhere since that whole section is killed by the adblocker, so it can't be put there... :\

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body:
As a "least worst solution", how about adding a html comment?

Probably, a fraction of people encountering the issue would have a look at the html source, thus it would help reducing the amount of reports.

See https://github.com/sphinx-doc/sphinx/issues/2719 for the method to implement this.

scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.
